subtitle: Level-Independent De-Esser
tagline: Finds sibilance by its sound rather than its level, and reduces it with a whole-signal dip or stereo-linked spectral cuts, keeping vocal air and diction intact.

body.lead: TB De-Esser detects sibilance by its character instead of a level threshold, so it reacts the same way in quiet and loud passages and needs no threshold setting. You tell it where to listen with FOCUS and how far to reduce with TAME.

body.p: The detector is a bank of six resonators weighted around `FOCUS`. The reduction is a separate spectral process, so the detector's filters do not color the output. `PROCESS` chooses whether the whole signal dips (WIDE) or only the detected sibilance band is cut (SPLIT). Both channels share one sibilance mask, so the stereo image stays stable.

ul: Level-independent, language-neutral sibilance detection with no threshold to set
FOCUS from 2.5 to 8 kHz moves the detector's sensitivity centre
TAME sets the maximum reduction, up to 20 dB
WIDE lowers the whole signal; SPLIT cuts only inside the detected sibilance band
Stereo-linked reduction for a stable image
LISTEN to hear the detector signal
ESS METER with gain reduction and detector confidence
10 factory presets, user presets, undo, and redo

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB De-Esser 1.0.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build (AU and VST3) is also version 1.0.0; small differences between platforms are possible.

ol: Insert TB De-Esser on a vocal or dialogue track. The defaults are `FOCUS` 2.50 kHz, `TAME` 6.0 dB, and `PROCESS` WIDE.
Play a passage with clear "s" and "sh" sounds and turn on `LISTEN` {{6}}. Move `FOCUS` {{2}} until you hear mostly the sibilant sounds.
Turn `LISTEN` off and raise `TAME` {{4}} until the sibilance sits right, watching the ESS METER {{3}}.
Compare WIDE and SPLIT with `PROCESS` {{5}}, and check the result against `BYPASS` {{7}}.

rows: Moves the resonator bank's sibilance sensitivity centre. It is not an EQ frequency for the output. Double-click to reset.
Sets the maximum gain reduction applied to detected sibilance. High values can over-reduce or smear the sound, so use only as much as you need.
WIDE lowers the whole signal while sibilance is detected. SPLIT applies stereo-linked spectral cuts only inside the detected sibilance band, so the lows and mids of the voice are left alone.
Monitors the Focus-weighted resonator-bank signal instead of the processed output. Use it to set FOCUS, then turn it off.
Compares processed and unprocessed audio. The bypassed signal is delayed by the same latency, so the comparison stays in time.

body.p: The ESS METER shows the current gain reduction in dB and how confidently the detector hears sibilance; its status line reads DETECT READY in the picture.

note.title: Latency
note.text: TB De-Esser has a fixed latency of 2048 samples (about 43 ms at 48 kHz), which it reports to the host for delay compensation. BYPASS and TAME 0 dB stay aligned with it, so A/B comparisons line up. Because of the latency it suits mixing and post-production rather than live monitoring.

tip.text: There is no threshold. Detection does not depend on level, so quiet and loud sibilants are treated alike; TAME sets how much they are reduced.

body.p: Step through presets with the arrows (hold to continue), or open the list to choose a factory or saved user preset. Save stores the current state as a .tbdeesser file in the TB_DeEsser user preset folder. Undo and Redo step through parameter and preset changes.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Lead vocal
recipes.use: Natural control of "s" sounds in a pop vocal.
steps: Raise TAME only until the sibilants stop jumping out.

recipes.title: Whisper and dialogue
recipes.use: Breathy, close speech with sharp sibilants.
steps: Use LISTEN to place FOCUS on the hiss of the consonants.

recipes.title: Acoustic guitar pick
recipes.use: Softer pick clicks without dulling the strings.
steps: Keep SPLIT so the body of the guitar is untouched.

recipes.title: Cymbal edge
recipes.use: Less splash in overheads or a drum bus.
steps: Move FOCUS higher if the cymbals still sound harsh.

rows: The voice sounds lispy or dull.
Lower TAME, or switch PROCESS to SPLIT so only the sibilance band is cut.
The whole vocal ducks on each "s".
That is how WIDE works. Use SPLIT for a more local cut.
Raise TAME, and check FOCUS with LISTEN.
The detector reacts to the wrong sounds.
Turn on LISTEN and move FOCUS until you hear mostly the sibilants.
The sound is thin and strange.
LISTEN is on. Turn it off to hear the processed output.
The track is late against others.
TB De-Esser has 2048 samples of latency. Turn on delay compensation in your host; do not use it for live monitoring.
